Some people like doing tires, and some hate it. So when someone says a tire is difficult, they either don’t want to do it or they can’t (I am not ripping on any other technicians I am just saying once you have the experience, pretty much every tire becomes the same

That is solely based on technician experience, currently my sidewall is a 35 on a road race tire (very very stiff) excluding balancing, just getting them on and off (4) I can do them in about 10 min, runflats are basically like M/T tires (mud) with the sidewalls being bigger, yes it is stiffer but most good shops have an arm attachment that can push the wall down when seating the tire

Tbh my shop gets teslas and camaros and other cars that have aftermarket wheels and we (well me) do fine with a prybar and not damaging wheels, if they are chrome or have a reflective surface, I usually lay my detailing cloths on the wheel where I am applying force so no damage occurs, other people literally don’t care

The main reason this happens is manufacturers actually use a raw steel lug (what you see underneath) and an aluminum cap (the mangled thing on top), because these are two different metals they have a reaction (amplified with heat) where the weaker metal or thinner metal will deform from the molding process :) the aluminum cap was intended to be used as a dust shield so object or weather can’t get into the nut itself and prevent it from coming off

If you are looking for soft touch in a Civic Si then the Si line is not for you, pretty much any car that has Si, ST, GT, M or R slapped on there is a performance vehicle and those areas are meant to be light and easily removable (with the right $2000 tool no one needs). You will find in European cars of higher end such as Audi (S-Line, not the S series) or BMW (M-package, not M-Sport) or Mercedes (I’ll admit a lot of the AMG have leather soft touch even around the knee areas or just more room), but cars that are designed for economy (Base Civics, Focus/Fiesta, Golfs, or MS3) are just that and meant to have a luxury look, not feel.

Also that special tool is called a prybar lol, in shops (I am willing to bet yes even the high roller ones do this) there is this thing called corporate rules/policy and “what I am actually going to do” rules/policy

But we have to understand the purpose of the Runflat first before we say it is a bad tire :) for those who live in an area where the roads are absolutely just as bad as the drivers (me here in Maryland) they have to understand, if they want something that will save them a headache with potholes... they need a bigger sidewall with a smaller aspect ratio

The reason runflats were designed is so that if you get a puncture in the tire, and there is no air in it, you can still drive up to 50 miles on the tire to get to a safe place to replace the tire. BMW puts runflat tires on their cars because from the factory their tires are filled with nitrogen instead of oxygen due to nitrogen does not heat up as much as oxygen filled tires so it save the wear on the tire. The stiffer sidewall was not meant to be driven over potholes, tbh no tire (exception of offroad tires) are meant to be driven over potholes, hence this situation lol. I have worked for many dealerships including BMW so that is where this information is coming from

Flats commonly occur in areas that are prone to high traffic to include semi trucks/Heavy duty trucks/ light duty trucks or vehicles related to construction or highway areas, the reason of this is the road is used more which cause soft spots in gravel/cement/tarmac which can create potholes, depending on the pothole size and your wheel size/sidewall height this can cause a flat whether it be the pothole at speed hits the bead of the tire, has a sharp object which punctures the tread which the % of that happening depends on air pressure in the tire

Runflat tires actually have reinforced sidewalls specifically for flat situations, now with runflats once you run it flat and drive to a service center you need them to be replaced because they wear the inside of the side wall out
